Q2752831.label: 1976 Cuban parliamentary election
Q2752831.summary: Indirect parliamentary elections were held in Cuba on 2 November 1976, the first since the Cuban Revolution.

Q5892927.label: 1980 Honduran Constituent Assembly election
Q5892927.summary: Constituent Assembly elections were held in Honduras on 20 April 1980. In July the Assembly elected Policarpo Paz García as president.

Q131703615.label: 2026 Costa Rican general election
Q131703615.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 1 February 2026 to elect the president, two vice-presidents, and all 57 deputies of the Legislative Assembly.

Q4393791.label: Liechtenstein fire insurance referendum, 1926
Q4393791.summary: A referendum on fire insurance was held in Liechtenstein on 7 February 1926. Voters were asked whether a state insurance scheme for fire damage should be established. The proposal was rejected by 66% of voters.

Q728895.label: Panagis Tsaldaris
Q728895.summary: Panagis Tsaldaris was a Greek politician who served as Prime Minister of Greece twice. He was a revered conservative politician and leader for many years (1922–1936) of the conservative People's Party in the period before World War II. He was the husband of Lina Tsaldari, a Greek suffragist, member of Parliament, and the Minister for Social Welfare.

Q81215.label: Petar Stoyanov
Q81215.summary: Petar Stefanov Stoyanov is a Bulgarian statesman and politician who served as the president of Bulgaria from 1997 to 2002. A member of the Union of Democratic Forces, he won the second democratic election in modern Bulgarian history. Throughout Stoyanov’s presidency, Bulgaria made substantial progress in its efforts of joining NATO and the European Union.

Q18015039.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Lithuania on 29 June 2014. Q65047871.label: 1990 Chadian coup d'état
Q65047871.summary: The 1990 Chadian coup d'état took place on 1 December 1990 when the forces of the Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS), a Libyan–backed rebel group under the leadership of General Idriss Déby, entered the Chadian capital N'Djamena unopposed. The MPS troops entered Chad by crossing the Sudanese border three weeks earlier.

Q28479.label: Kumanovo Agreement
Q28479.desc: agreement that concluded the Kosovo war
Q28479.summary: The Military Technical Agreement, also known as the Kumanovo Agreement, signed between the International Security Force (KFOR) and the Governments of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia, was an accord concluded on 9 June 1999 in Kumanovo, Macedonia.

mentions.c: North Macedonia: Treaty signed: Kumanovo Agreement

Q4808511.label: assassination of Hrant Dink
Q4808511.summary: The prominent Turkish-Armenian journalist Hrant Dink was assassinated in Istanbul on 19 January 2007. Dink was a newspaper editor who had written and spoken about the Armenian genocide and was well known for his efforts for reconciliation between Turks and Armenians and his advocacy of human and minority rights in Turkey.

mentions.c: Turkey: Assassination: assassination of Hrant Dink

Q28094271.label: 2017 Istanbul nightclub attack
Q28094271.desc: terrorist mass shooting that occurred at a nightclub in the Beşiktaş district of Istanbul, Turkey, on 1 January 2017
Q28094271.summary: The Istanbul nightclub shooting was a mass shooting that occurred on 1 January 2017 around 01:18 local time, in which a terrorist shot and killed 39 people and wounded 79 others at the Reina nightclub in the Ortaköy neighborhood of Istanbul, Turkey, where hundreds had been celebrating New Year's Day.

mentions.c: Turkey: Terrorist attack: 2017 Istanbul nightclub attack

Q48852287.label: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
Q48852287.desc: multilateral free trade agreement and successor to TPP
Q48852287.wiki: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership
Q48852287.summary: The Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), previously proposed as the TPP11 is a multilateral trade agreement that consists of twelve members states, spans over five continents and covers nearly 600 million people.

mentions.c: International: Treaty signed: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership

Q111017791.label: Siege of Mariupol
Q111017791.desc: battle in the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine
Q111017791.summary: The siege of Mariupol began on 24 February 2022, as part of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, and lasted until 20 May. It saw fighting between the Russian Armed Forces and the Ukrainian Armed Forces for control over the city of Mariupol in southeastern Ukraine.

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine

Q136309567.label: Operation Strike
Q136309567.summary: Operation Strike was the last ground attack by the Allied forces of the First Army against the Italian and German forces in Tunis, Cape Bon and Bizerte, the last Axis bridgeheads in North Africa, during the Tunisian campaign of the Second World War. The offensive was launched only a week after the end of Operation Vulcan, in which the Axis forces had been severely weakened and hemmed in against the coast but the Allies were unable to break out.

Q115816255.label: Battle of Sarantaporos
Q115816255.summary: The Battle of Sarantaporos on 21 June 1943 was a successful ambush by the guerrillas of the Greek People's Liberation Army (ELAS) against a column of the German 117th Jäger Division. The ambush, carried out as part of Operation Animals, was one of the most successful operations against the Germans during the Axis occupation of Greece.

Q4873023.label: Battle of the Tennis Court
Q4873023.desc: part of the Battle of Kohima in North East India in 1944
Q4873023.summary: The Battle of the Tennis Court was part of the wider Battle of Kohima that was fought in North East India from 4 April to 22 June 1944 during the Burma Campaign of the Second World War. The Japanese advance into India was halted at Kohima in April 1944 and Garrison Hill, on a long wooded ridge on a high ridge west of the village, was, according to the Commonwealth War Graves Commission the scene of "perhaps the most bitter fighting of the whole Burma campaign when a small Commonwealth force held out against repeated attacks by a Japanese Division".

Q138448191.label: Bombing of Macau
Q138448191.summary: The Bombing of Macau was a series of air raids conducted by the United States against the neutral Portuguese colony of Macau during the final months of World War II. The attacks, carried out between January and July 1945, were part of broader U.S. naval operations in the South China Sea and were the only direct military attacks on the enclave during the war.

Q7097151.label: Operation Hump
Q7097151.img: US 1 503rd paratrooper Operation Hump SVN November 1965.PNG
Q7097151.summary: Operation Hump was a search and destroy operation initiated by United States and Australian forces on 5 November 1965, during the Vietnam War.

Q3030335.label: Operation Hammer
Q3030335.desc: 2007 Coalition operation during the War in Afghanistan
Q3030335.summary: Operation Hammer was a British-led NATO operation in the southern Helmand province of Afghanistan. The Task Force level offensive, codenamed 'Chakush' or 'Hammer', began in the early hours of July 24, 2007 in the area between Hyderabad and Mirmandab, north-east of Gereshk. The operation continued the momentum towards expelling Taliban forces from areas of the Upper Gereshk Valley in Helmand province.

Q135984959.label: Iraqi intervention in the Syrian Civil War
Q135984959.desc: Iraqi state and militia involvement in the Syrian Civil War
Q135984959.wiki: Iraqi involvement in the Syrian civil war
Q135984959.summary: Iraq has been involved in the Syrian civil war by launching airstrikes against the Islamic State in coordination with the Ba'athist Syrian government. Although the actions of the Iraqi Armed Forces were limited to anti-ISIS activities, pro-Iranian Iraqi Shi'ite militias have notably fought on the side of the Syrian government more openly, launching attacks against Syrian opposition militias and American forces under Iranian allegiance.

Q2385727.label: Battle of Rastan
Q2385727.summary: A second battle between the Syrian Army and the Free Syrian Army for control of the city of Rastan took place from 29 January to 5 February 2012. Located in Homs Governorate, Rastan is a city of 60,000 residents. The FSA captured Rastan after days of intense fighting, according to residents and the opposition.

Q18121535.label: Opération Chammal
Q18121535.desc: French military operation in Iraq and Syria which started on 19 September 2014
Q18121535.summary: Opération Chammal is a French military operation in Iraq and Syria launched to help curtail the expansion of the Islamic State and to support the Iraqi Army. Its name comes from the Shamal, a northwesterly wind that blows over Iraq and the Persian Gulf states.

Q28162879.label: 2016 Nassoumbou attack
Q28162879.desc: battle of the islamist insurgency in Burkina Faso
Q28162879.summary: On 16 December 2016, jihadists from Ansarul Islam and the Islamic State in the Greater Sahara attacked a Burkinabe army outpost in Nassoumbou, Soum Province, Burkina Faso, killing twelve soldiers. The attack was the first claimed by Ansarul Islam, Burkina Faso's first homegrown jihadist movement that formed a month prior.
